_comment: Generated by `cargo test -p axiam-opaque --test vectors_test`. Do not edit by hand. Re-sync into every SDK repository when it changes.

configuration._comment: RFC 9807's recommended configuration. An SDK MUST NOT accept a `suite` value it does not recognise, and MUST NOT let a server select primitives outside this table.

error_mapping.400_login_start: NetworkError (a malformed message is the SDK's own fault)
error_mapping.401_login_finish: AuthenticationError (wrong password, unknown identity, or expired session — indistinguishable by design)
error_mapping.404_login_start: OPAQUE disabled for this tenant, NOT 'no such user'
error_mapping.500_login_start: server misconfiguration: keys absent while policy is on
error_mapping._comment: How an SDK maps what it sees. `opaque_required` is the one that matters: mapping it to an authentication error would send a user off to reset a password that works, and would stop the SDK switching to the OPAQUE endpoints on its own.

ksf_wire_cases._comment: argon2id: memory_kib, iterations and parallelism present; scrypt fields absent, NOT zero.
scrypt: log_n, r and p present; argon2id fields absent.
An unrecognised KSF MUST be refused, never substituted. Substituting produces a well-formed randomized password that no AXIAM server agrees with, reported to the user as a wrong password.

utf8._comment: There is no shared password fixture, deliberately. The SRP file carried one because its vectors pinned `x`, which two implementations had to agree on; with one implementation there is nothing to agree about. What remains is the obligation: every SDK MUST drive a non-ASCII password through its binding, choosing its own, so that a binding handing the core its platform's default encoding fails in a test rather than for one unlucky user.
